subject: Invoice originator escalation: legacy EDI fallback, email consent, and remit contact rotation

Subject: Invoice creation question: who should originate? legacy EDI fallback

Hi Aditya,

Quick question as we get close to contract signature: who will be the invoice originator for Greenline invoices? Our AP stack still relies on a legacy EDI batch for some subsidiaries, but our central AP team needs an emailed PDF copy for reconciliation.

Two constraints:
- For the EU entity we need VAT tagging on the invoice (reverse-charge info).
- Our legacy EDI vendor (Elena Park, cc'd) requires a field map and a weekly batch window if Redwood will push EDI.

Can Redwood either originate the invoice (preferred from our internal stance) or do we need to continue originating and have you send the copy? Also confirm what remit/contact will appear on the invoice — we want to avoid routing delays.

Thanks,
Maria

Subject: Re: Invoice creation question: who should originate? legacy EDI fallback

Hi Maria — thanks for flagging. Happy to lay out a short options matrix so you can pick the path that fits Greenline's rollout. TL;DR: Redwood can be the invoice originator and support both portal push (preferred) and an EDI fallback during go-live.

Options we support (recommended order):
1) Redwood-originated via e-invoice portal + email copies to AP (recommended). Produces human-readable PDF + structured metadata (VAT tags, remit fields).
2) Redwood-originated EDI push (weekly batch) to your legacy vendor (Elena) — we require an EDI field map and a test window.
3) Greenline originate, Redwood sends an automated PDF copy to AP and stores canonical copy in the portal. Less control on our side for credits/adjusts.

To move forward we need three things from your side:
- Confirm primary remit/contact name + email (who should appear on remittance instructions).
- VAT/Tax IDs per billing entity (EU reverse-charge flag if applicable).
- Preference for go-live: portal-first with EDI fallback or EDI-first with portal copies.

Attached: sample_invoice_Greenline_202611.pdf (PDF) showing fields we populate, and edi_field_map_v2.csv — quick notes in the file header. Connor is looped for mapping and cutover schedule; Kimberly will own AP contact mapping on our side.

If helpful I can send a one-page mutual action plan once you confirm the preferred path. Proposed interim: Redwood originates via portal, we also queue an EDI batch for your legacy vendor during the first 30 days so AP receives both formats.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Best,
Maria
From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Invoice originator escalation: next steps & mutual action plan

Maria / AP team — great, thanks for confirming. Action items below (we'll open a shared folder + HubSpot MAP):

1) Redwood will be the official invoice originator for Greenline (portal-first) starting on contract go-live date. We will include VAT reverse-charge flag for EU bill-to entity and display the remit contact as "Greenline Health AP / ap-team@greenlineinc.com".
2) EDI parallel run: Connor will coordinate a weekly outbound batch for the first 30 days to Elena's endpoint. Connor — can you propose the test window (we typically do 2x tests in lower-case environment, then a production handshake)?
3) Kimberly to confirm invoice field mapping for your AP system and validate whether AP requires PO-level line splits.
4) Greenline: provide final EDI endpoint URL and sample 997 acknowledgements (Elena), plus confirmation of final go-live date.

I've created a short MAP and uploaded it here: https://drive.redwood.com/Greenline/Invoices/2026 (see file "Greenline_MAP_invoice_originator_20261126.docx"). Also linking the HubSpot deal so our CS and finance teams can track: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/DL-9321

If no objections I'll mark the MAP as "accepted pending EDI test" on Friday EOD and schedule the first test run Monday morning.

Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the EDI test.

Cheers,
